title: Hierarchical soft-reserve KV GPU compaction and batch-smoothing
creator: Ava Martinez
summary: Introduce a hierarchical, workload-aware soft-reserve allocator for the KV cache with epochal compaction windows tied to the continuous-batching pipeline. The goal is to reduce long-tail fragmentation on multi-tenant GPUs while bounding token-latency impact during background reclamation.
background: We see recurring fragmentation on long-lived KV pools when workloads exhibit bursty sequence length distributions and ephemeral hotspots. Existing compaction passes either run opportunistically (insufficiently proactive) or aggressively (causing token latency spikes). Continuous batching complicates matters because batch composition changes allocation pressure and KV residency patterns in sub-second windows.
goals: (1) Bring down GPU memory overhead due to fragmentation by >= 18% on synthetic hotspot workloads. (2) Keep 99th-percentile per-request token latency regression < 4% during steady-state compaction. (3) Provide observable signals and knobs to tune compaction aggressiveness per deployment tier.
non_goals: Replacing the runtime allocator. This work builds on top of existing slab/chunk allocator primitives and focuses on eviction/reservation and compaction scheduling. Not addressing multi-host shard rebalances in this ticket.
proposed_solution_overview: Add a three-tier reservation model (Transient, Stable, Strategic) that maps to dynamic soft-reserve quotas in the KV pool. Use an epochal compaction controller that aligns micro-compaction windows to batching microepochs. Introduce a KV residency score for entries and a lightweight pointer indirection layer to enable cheap micro-relocations instead of full rewrites.
design_details:
- Reservation tiers:
  - Transient: small, per-request prefix cache; high churn; zero compaction priority.
  - Stable: mid-term allocations for repeated prefixes; moderate compaction priority.
  - Strategic: long-lived pinned entries (LLMs pinned prompts/anchors); low eviction frequency but marked for batch-time opportunistic relocation.

- Epochal compaction controller:
  - Define a compaction epoch aligned to the batching window (typical: 200ms microepoch).
  - Each epoch computes fragmentation score per slab (external fragmentation ratio + vacancy runs).
  - If score > threshold and GPU utilization < util_target, schedule micro-coalesces sized to avoid increasing tail latency beyond budget.

- Batch-smoothing integration:
  - Track per-batch KV cache touch patterns and use them to create relocation working sets that align with upcoming batch composition predictions.
  - Prefer relocating entries that are unlikely to be referenced in the immediate next N microepochs.

- Lightweight indirection & relocation:
  - Introduce a one-word indirection table per slot (small fixed-size table) to allow moving backing pages while keeping logical slot IDs stable.
  - Micro-relocations update indirection atomically and are bounded to single-page moves where possible to avoid large memcopies.

- Compaction pacing heuristics:
  - Rate-limit copy bandwidth per GPU based on a latency budget derived from recent P99 token latencies.
  - Backoff if batch latency increases > 3% over baseline for two consecutive epochs.

- Eviction & admission policy:
  - Admission favors Stable entries with high recurrence score.
  - Transient entries are eligible for immediate eviction under pressure.
  - Strategic entries can be softly reserved for a configurable fraction of the pool; expiration is policy-driven.
implementation_steps:
1) Instrument KV pools to emit fragmentation and vacancy-run histograms (ENG-63102 has related metrics).
2) Implement tier annotations on allocations and API to pin/promote/demote slots.
3) Add epochal compaction controller tied to batching scheduler.
4) Implement indirection table and safe atomic swap for micro-relocations.
5) Add compaction pacing controller and latency feedback loop.
6) Integrate admission logic with existing cache placement.
7) End-to-end tests and microbench harness.
8) Rollout canary + telemetry validation + gradual ramp to 100%.
telemetry_and_alerting: Emit the following signals: fragmentation_ratio_per_slab, vacancy_run_length_histogram, relocation_bytes/sec, compaction_epochs_triggered, average_compaction_window_ms, P50/P95/P99 batch latency pre/post compaction, eviction_rate_by_tier. Create dashboard and set alerts: fragmentation_ratio > 0.25 for 5m (warning), relocation_bytes/sec > baseline*5 (investigate).
acceptance_criteria:
- Integration tests demonstrate relocation correctness under concurrency with no KV loss.
- Synthetic hotspot benchmark shows >= 18% reduction in fragmentation overhead vs baseline with similar throughput.
- Canary runs at 10% traffic show tail token latency regression < 3% and maximum memory reclaimed matches model.
- Telemetry surfaces per-tier utilization and compaction impact on latency.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for indirection table correctness and atomic swap.
- Race tests with concurrent reads/writes and relocations.
- Microbench: bursty sequence-length workload, steady-state and warm-cache scenarios.
- End-to-end: multi-tenant sim with continuous batching enabled.
- Canary: 10% traffic for 24h, then 50% for 48h, validate telemetry and error budgets.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable epochal compaction controller with conservative thresholds on a single region (10% traffic). Phase 2: increase to 50% with more aggressive compaction windows. Phase 3: full rollout after 72h stable telemetry and no customer impact. Feature flag controls: compaction_enabled, compaction_aggressiveness, tier_quota_overrides.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Compaction causes unexpected P99 spikes. Mitigation: immediate global kill-switch and per-region auto-backoff tied to latency regressions.
- Risk: Indirection adds read latency. Mitigation: keep indirection locality in L1 and use CPU/GPU caches for indirection lookups; measure overhead < 0.5% per-token.
- Risk: Incorrect eviction policy hurting cache hit-rate. Mitigation: shadow-mode admission for first rollout and offline replay validation.
